fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Hollywood Dreams to Truth Comedy", "body": "Benny grew up in Hollywood with two actor parents and chased the acting dream from childhood into his late twenties or early thirties, along the way noticing inconsistencies in official stories, questioning authority, and reaching people through comedy in ways that conversation and link sharing could not. He later tried poetry at a conference without telling anybody and now performs at truth-based conferences. He says most people in Hollywood have no idea what they are participating in, which Chance ties to the compartmentalization every mafia runs on, and Benny says it took him a long time to see that real success is simple: friends, love and family."}, {"title": "Who Is Really Doing the Conspiring?", "body": "Asked to define the grand conspiracy, Benny describes forces that want people distracted, unhealthy, dependent and divided, working through toxicity on every level, and he urges detoxifying physically, spiritually and emotionally. Chance turns the word around: a conspiracy is people acting in unison, so anyone willfully ignorant of what is harming them becomes a co-conspirator, and he casts levity as the opposite of that weight. Benny closes the first hour with his poem They, written for the curveball question of who they are, which runs through a long list of suspects before answering with we, us, and you and me."}, {"title": "Hope in a Year of Distance", "body": "Benny's positive story of 2020 is his newborn son, whose arrival in the middle of the pandemic he came to see as exactly the right time. Watching a newborn who shows only discomfort or contentment convinced him people are born needing one another, which is why he calls social distancing so destructive. Chance recalls a child hiding from a masked grandmother he did not recognize, and Benny, a self-described apocaloptimist, argues that every push of an agenda also liberates people, that the future is unwritten, and that homesteading is his answer."}, {"title": "Labels, Buzzwords and Word Magic", "body": "Benny's comedy channel Joy Camp was listed as far right in a late November analysis of YouTube echo chambers, which he says shows the label is not rooted in any truth, while joking that he is honored to make the cut. Chance argues society labels something and that makes it so, noting that a movement of people sharing information gets branded an echo chamber. Benny says news-trained audiences react like Pavlov's dogs to buzzwords, calling it programming through language, and Chance, whose podcast keeps bringing him back to word magic, singles out legalese, which he frames as an unchanging priestly language beside a vulgar tongue that keeps shifting."}, {"title": "Parrhesia and the Art of Planting Seeds", "body": "Benny spent six months building Parrhesia, a course named for a word he says means free speech, aimed at conquering the fear of speaking, finding a creative voice, and no longer being the conspiracy theorist who fire hoses people with information. You open a door and let someone walk through, he says, and the victory is when they reach the idea on their own and give you no credit. Chance likens it to scattering seeds on fertile ground instead of glaring at one in rocky soil, and Benny adds that most people resist conspiracy because they cannot accept that level of deception."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Benny Wills is a truth focused poet and Youtube personality, well known for his work on the comedic conspiracy channel JoyCamp. In this meeting of the minds, we talk about Benny's journey, the grand conspiracy and how to detox ourselves from it's poisons, what it's like to have a newborn in 2020, and much more. Benny also shares some profound poetry!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Living With One Foot in the System", "body": "Benny describes the Social Security system and the legal persona as a smoke and mirrors act, a legal fiction, yet admits that living as an impenetrable free man on the land takes absolute dedication he has not given it. His answer is to stay stealthy, keep one foot in the door, and wrestle with the beast in order to tame it. Chance frames the legal persona as a copy without an original, and the conversation later returns to the idea of a consent-based reality, where knowing how not to consent, and having food growing on your own property, becomes essential."}, {"title": "Forecasting a Hard 2021", "body": "Asked about the Operation Warp Speed vaccines, Benny suspects the first round will seem harmless and that some later event could corner hesitant people, pointing to Ice Age Farmer's warning that a cyberattack on the food supply might tie groceries to vaccination. A USA Today headline assuring readers that trial reports of Bell's palsy are not as scary as they sound gets roundly mocked. The pair weigh Klaus Schwab's cyberattack forecast and the Rockefeller Lockstep document, whose next scenario was Hack Attack, before Chance reads 2021 as a two to one ritual echoing the twin towers. These are their views, offered as speculation."}, {"title": "Scripture as Metaphor, Not Literal History", "body": "Benny calls 2020 a come to Jesus year, crediting Dylan Saccoccio and Clint Richardson, whose work reads the crucifixion as notice of the legal death of the straw man. Chance argues literalism divides people, that a historical Jesus can be turned into an inheritable corporate office, and that the stars are among the most self-evident parts of reality to learn from. Benny recalls Cal Washington asking a room who had actually read the Bible, and warns of cognitive dissonance in praising God while eating GMO food, while Chance says idolatry makes you idle, and faith itself gets reframed as acting in good faith."}, {"title": "Lockdowns Through the Lens of Coercion", "body": "Chance walks through a Corbett Report and James Evan Pilato year-end comparison between a 1956 study of communist coercive methods and the COVID measures: isolation, monopolization of perception, induced debility, threats, trivial demands, degradation and occasional indulgences like partying in Wuhan. Benny calls it brilliant and notes that the mask hesitant are cast as selfish asymptomatic super spreaders, even quoting Bill Gates blaming them. His response is to walk into stores calmly and unmasked, with no rebel energy, and Chance adds that the best case for any of it is to crush at life, which Benny sums up as being undeniable."}, {"title": "Courage in the Truth Community", "body": "Benny names the voices he follows, including James Corbett, True Stream Media, KJ Osborne, Owen Benjamin, Max Igan and Mark Passio, and urges listeners to forgive creators who are sometimes wrong in real time. Having met many of his heroes at conferences, and holding an MFA in acting, he says none struck him as fakes, and that the real trap is calling everyone controlled opposition. He shows his course students the nastiest comments he has received, arguing that censorship is the worst they can do, and that fear should be wrestled with and used as fuel rather than conquered, while Chance suggests reframing anxiety as anticipation."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Bringing humor to the situation, it's not just something that will maybe hold someone's attention better, but it actually is a healing mechanism.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Everything is toxic, and we have to really be conscious of how to detoxify ourselves, physically, spiritually, emotionally, everything.", "author": "Benny Wills", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/4200e523-7df2-4c06-8371-61f36ac2efd7/BENNY-WILLS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We're co-conspirators every time that we are willfully ignorant of participating in things that are harming us.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Even someone who claims to be an introvert or they like being alone, they still crave some kind of friendship, some kind of companionship, because that's what we are born needing.", "author": "Benny Wills", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/4200e523-7df2-4c06-8371-61f36ac2efd7/BENNY-WILLS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Success is really much more simple.
